'''Stephen Ray Wiggins''' (born 1959) is a [[Cherokee]]-[[United States|American]] prolific applied mathematician in the fields of [[nonlinear dynamics]], [[chaos theory]] and [[Nonlinear system|nonlinear phenomena]]. His wide range of outstanding contributions include [[Lagrangian mechanics|Lagrangian]] aspects of fluid dynamics and reaction dynamics in [[theoretical chemistry]]. He is currently a full professor at the Hetao Institute of Mathematics and Interdisciplinary Sciences, [[China]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stephen Wiggins|url=http://en.himis-sz.cn/ry_36/120.html|access-date=4 August 2026|website=Hetao Institute of Mathematics and Interdisciplinary Sciences，HIMIS, Shenzhen-Hong Kong International Science Park }}</ref> and honorary professor in [[Bristol University]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Stephen Wiggins|url=https://www.bristolmathsresearch.org/staff-profile/professor-stephen-wiggins/|access-date=4 August 2026|website=Bristol School of Mathematics Research Profile}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Wiggins was born in [[Oklahoma City]], [[Oklahoma]] in 1959, and has two younger siblings. He is enrolled as a citizen of the [[Cherokee Nation]].{{Citation needed|date=March 2026}} He received a BSc in physics and mathematics from [[Pittsburg State University]] in 1980, an MA in mathematics and an MSc in physics from the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]] in 1983, and a PhD in [[Theoretical mechanics|theoretical]] and [[applied mechanics]] from [[Cornell University]] in 1985. He also attended the [[Open University]] in [[Great Britain]], where he earned a [[Bachelor of Laws]], with honors, in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web|last=ORCID|title=Stephen Wiggins (0000-0002-0780-0911)|url=http://orcid.org/0000-0002-0780-0911|access-date=2020-09-13|website=orcid.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Stephen Wiggins|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Stephen_Wiggins|access-date=13 September 2020|website=ResearchGate}}</ref>

==Academic career and field of study==
Wiggins was influenced heavily by his PhD advisor [[Philip Holmes]]. His dissertation was on "Slowly Varying Oscillators."<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Stephen Ray Wiggins|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=11962|access-date=21 September 2020|website=Mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> From 1987 to 2001, he was a professor at [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kovačič|first1=Gregor|last2=Wiggins|first2=Stephen|date=1992-06-15|title=Orbits homoclinic to resonances, with an application to chaos in a model of the forced and damped sine-Gordon equation|journal=Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena|language=en|volume=57|issue=1|pages=185–225|doi=10.1016/0167-2789(92)90092-2|issn=0167-2789}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Smith|first=Douglas L.|date=2002|title=Next Exit 0.5 Million Kilometers|url=https://calteches.library.caltech.edu/685/2/Exit.pdf|journal=Engineering & Science|volume=4|page=12|quote=…Steve Wiggins [a Caltech professor from 1987 to2001].}}</ref> He is an emeritus professor of applied mathematics in [[University of Bristol]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bristol|first=University of|title=People Profiler navigation|url=https://www.bristol.ac.uk/maths/people/stephen-r-wiggins/index.html|access-date=2020-09-21|website=www.bristol.ac.uk|language=en-GB}}</ref> where he was the head of the mathematics department from 2004 until 2008 and was the school research director.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=2017-05-13|title=Steve Wiggins|url=https://champsproject.com/steve-wiggins/|access-date=2020-09-21|website=CHAMPS|language=en}}</ref> As of August 2020 Wiggins had 12 PhD students and 60 academic descendants.<ref name=":1" /> In 2026, he took a faculty role in Hetao Institute of Mathematics and Interdisciplinary Sciences, initiated by [[Shing-Tung Yau]], as a professor and retaining his emeritus role in Bristol.

Wiggins has contributed in many different areas of [[applied mathematics]], science, and [[engineering]] using applied and computational dynamics as the framework for his approach and analysis.<ref name=":2" />

His current focus is on developing the [[phase space]] approach to chemical reaction dynamics in the setting of the CHAMPS (Chemistry and Mathematics in Phase Space) project.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> Previously he has established a successful US-UK-Spain research network in building a foundational connection between applied mathematics and theoretical chemistry with [[Turgay Uzer]].<ref name="The geometry of reaction dynamics">{{Cite journal|last1=Uzer|first1=Turgay|last2= Jaffé |first2=C.|last3= Palacián |first3=J.|last4= Yanguas Palacián |first4=P.|last5=Wiggins|first5=Stephen|title=The geometry of reaction dynamics|url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1088/0951-7715/15/4/301|journal=Nonlinearity|language=en|volume=15|issue=4|page=957}}</ref>

==Honors==
Wiggins received the [[Presidential Young Investigator Award|Presidential Young Investigators Award]] from the [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF) in August 1989.<ref>{{Cite web|date=27 May 1992|title=NSF 92-55 Directory of Awards, Engineering Directorate|url=https://www.nsf.gov/pubs/stis1992/nsf9255/nsf9255.txt?org=NSF|access-date=1 October 2020|website=NSF.gov|archive-date=21 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221021150019/https://www.nsf.gov/pubs/stis1992/nsf9255/nsf9255.txt?org=NSF|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

He was a [[Stanislaw Ulam|Stanislaw M. Ulam]] Visiting Scholar at the Center for Nonlinear Studies, [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]], from 1989 to 1990.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Center for Nonlinear Studies|url=https://cnls.lanl.gov/External/Ulam.php|access-date=2020-10-01|website=cnls.lanl.gov}}</ref>

He received the [[Office of Naval Research|US Office of Naval Research]] (ONR) Young Investigator Award in [[Cornelius Lanczos|Applied Analysis]] in 1989.<ref>{{Cite web|author1-link=Jinqiao Duan|last=Duan|first=Jinqiao|date=29 March 2019|title=Big Data and the Dynamical Systems Approach: New Directions and Applications (chemistry, geophysical fluid dynamics) in Applied Mathematics|url=http://math.iit.edu/pipermail/grads/2019-March/003040.html|access-date=2020-10-01}}{{Dead link|date=January 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
